# Business Requirements Document (BRD)

> Captures the **why** and **what** in business language. No schemas, no SQL.
> If a business stakeholder can't read and approve it, it isn't a BRD.

## 1. Overview
- **Title:**
- **Author / Date / Version:**
- **Sponsor (who is accountable):**
- **Status:** Draft | In Review | Approved

## 2. Business Problem & Goal
- **Problem statement** (1–2 sentences):
- **Business goal / desired outcome:**
- **Decision(s) this enables:**

## 3. Stakeholders
| Role | Name | Interest | Sign-off? |
|------|------|----------|-----------|
|      |      |          |           |

## 4. Scope
- **In scope:**
- **Out of scope (explicitly):**
- **Assumptions:**

## 5. Success Criteria
- How we'll know this succeeded (measurable):

## 6. Constraints & Deadlines
- **Timeline / hard dates:**
- **Budget / tooling constraints:**

## 7. Open Questions
-

<summary>Filled example (click to expand)</summary>

**Title:** Sales Rep Performance & Coaching Dashboard
**Sponsor:** VP Sales (accountable) · **Status:** In Review

**Problem:** Sales leadership has no consistent, timely view of individual rep
performance, so underperformers are identified late — usually only at
quarter-end reviews, too late to intervene.
**Goal:** Enable managers to spot reps trending below target *within the
quarter* so coaching happens in weeks 4–8, not week 13.
**Decision enabled:** Which reps get a targeted coaching plan this month.

**Success criteria:** All 6 managers use it weekly within 30 days; ≥3 at-risk
reps identified before week 8; numbers reconcile to the official quarter-end
bookings report (±0%).

See [the full methodology](../stakeholder-to-technical-requirements.md#41-business-requirements-doc-brd)
for the complete filled example.

</details>
